note: The founders skipped psoriasis animal models and went to a human proof-of-concept on Th17 biology; the gut and Candida harms that followed had been flagged by mouse knockout work that the sponsor's own Crohn's trial still called unexpected.
label: Psoriasis (IL-17A)

engagement.model: IL-17-stimulated human keratinocytes (in vitro gene set)
engagement.note: Ixekizumab ablated the in vitro-defined IL-17/TNF gene set in lesional biopsies by 2 weeks; DEFB4/LCN2/CXCL1 suppression tracked epidermal improvement.
engagement.short: Keratinocyte IL-17 gene set fell in lesions
engagement.quote: Overall, these data suggest that: 1) synergistic and additive effects of IL-17 and TNF on mRNA abundance for specific genes occurs in vivo in psoriasis lesions …
engagement.judgement: Quote is the first clause of a 41-word sentence. The cell-culture model under-predicted: the paper says rapid reversal of epidermal hyperplasia and suppression of Th1/Th22 cytokines were 'not predicted from pathway models'; direction right, breadth larger. No earlier use of this model for an anti-IL-17A antibody was verified, so the strip opens here rather than with an untested entry.

dose.note: Secukinumab binds primate but not rodent IL-17A, so cynomolgus carried all PK/TK and repeat-dose toxicology; in the IND by 2009.
dose.short: Cynomolgus is the only tox species
dose.quote: Secukinumab crossreacts with cynomolgus, rhesus and marmoset monkey IL-17A, but not with rodent IL-17A, making the cynomolgus monkey the most appropriate nonclinical species.
dose.judgement: Year is the IND review date the FDA document cites (IND 100418, 2009-05-28); the source itself was posted with the 2015 approval. FDA review signed 2014-08-07, posted with the 2015-01 approval.

dose.note: FDA: the clinical 300 mg dose (5 mg/kg) is 1/10 of the cynomolgus NOAEL and, as that margin implied, did not lower lymphocytes in patients.
dose.short: Cyno NOAEL margin held in patients
dose.quote: Clinical dosing at 1/10th the NOAEL (300 mg/60 kg = 5 mg/kg) did not significantly decrease total lymphocytes.
dose.reason: Cyno NOAEL margin held; no PD target compared
dose.judgement: This is a toxicology exposure margin checked against patients, not an efficacy exposure or IL-17A occupancy target; no source compared a cynomolgus-derived efficacy exposure with patient PK/PD, so a stricter reading keeps dose untested. FDA review signed 2014-08-07, posted with the 2015-01 approval.

efficacy.note: First psoriasis-like mouse model shown to need the IL-23/IL-17 axis, by IL-17 receptor knockout rather than an antibody.
efficacy.quote: IMQ-induced dermatitis was partially dependent on the presence of T cells, whereas disease development was almost completely blocked in mice deficient for IL-23 or the IL-17 receptor, demonstrating a pivotal role of the IL-23/IL-17 axis.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level. Rizzo 2011 (doi 10.4049/jimmunol.1001001, epub Dec 2010) then showed a blocking anti-IL-17A antibody abolished IL-23-induced epidermal hyperplasia in mice; no source compares either mouse model with PASI, and the FDA review filed no psoriasis model because secukinumab does not bind rodent IL-17A.

efficacy.model: Human proof-of-concept on Th17 biology and other-disease autoimmunity mouse models (CIA/EAE/EAU)
efficacy.note: Secukinumab's first-in-human trial tested the animal-model premise directly: one 3 mg/kg dose lowered PASI in 36 patients; no psoriasis animal model was in the chain.
efficacy.short: Human POC confirmed the IL-17A premise
efficacy.quote: These results support a role for IL-17A in the pathophysiology of diverse inflammatory diseases including psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and noninfectious uveitis.
efficacy.reason: Human POC matched Th17 premise; mouse unused
efficacy.judgement: Called same on the paper's own framing (abstract opens with IL-17A's effects 'in animal models of autoimmunity, including collagen-induced arthritis, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, and experimental autoimmune uveitis', then tests it in patients). Strictly the agreement is with mouse models of other diseases; Krueger 2012 notes mouse psoriasis models had favoured IL-22 over IL-17 as the hyperplasia driver. Abstract only (paywalled). Phase 3 (Langley 2014, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1314258, PASI 75 77-82% vs 4.5-4.9%, 'validating interleukin-17A as a therapeutic target'; ERASURE NCT01365455 results posted 2015-05-29) did not change status.

safety.model: Mouse IL-17A-deficient colitis and IL-17R-knockout oral-candidiasis models
safety.note: Transfer colitis worsened without IL-17A, and IL-17R-knockout mice could not clear oral Candida (Conti 2009): two harms flagged before any patient saw the class.
safety.short: Mouse gut and Candida harms flagged
safety.quote: Here we demonstrate IL-17A-mediated protection in the CD45RBhi transfer model of colitis.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level. Conti 2009 (doi 10.1084/jem.20081463) supplies the Candida half; neither mouse study dosed an anti-IL-17A antibody of the class, and secukinumab cannot be dosed in mice.

safety.model: Mouse colitis (IL-17A-deficient T-cell transfer) and anti-IL-17A oral-candidiasis models
safety.note: Secukinumab worsened Crohn's (ΔCDAI 49 favouring placebo) with 4 fungal infections vs 0; the authors invoke the gut-protective mouse models the title calls unexpected.
safety.short: Crohn's worsened and Candida rose, as mice said
safety.quote: It is possible that blocking of IL-17A may interfere with a protective function of IL-17A in the intestine.
safety.reason: Mouse gut and Candida harms held
safety.judgement: Comparison population was Crohn's patients, not psoriasis; the psoriasis-population harm is on the Cosentyx label (dailymed setid 77c4b13e-7df3-42d4-81db-3d0cddb7f67a, 5.4: 'Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) exacerbations, in some cases serious and/or leading to discontinuation of COSENTYX, occurred in COSENTYX treated subjects during clinical trials in PsO...'; Candida 1.2% vs 0.3%). The filed 26-week cynomolgus toxicology was silent on IBD and would score contra on its own; the colitis prediction was literature, never filed. The Candida model was filed: FDA review section 10 reports a sponsor mouse oral-candidiasis study in which anti-IL-17A-treated mice failed to clear infection by day 4. registry_date is the core trial CAIN457A2202 (NCT00584740, results posted 2015-03-31); the paper cites the extension NCT01009281 (results posted 2021-07-12).
